I proposed names for the eight niches. They're waiting in the STAnnotator review window and only apply when you click Accept.

|---|---|---|
| N1 | muscularis | 66% smooth muscle, the deepest niche (~1.8 mm from the epithelium); the muscle bands on the H&E |
| N2 | submucosa | blood vessel ECs, trophocytes, pericytes and macrophages, ~1.2 mm deep; the vessel-rich loose tissue |
| N3 | lamina propria | telocytes, trophocytes, CD8 T cells and Tregs right under the epithelium (~25 µm) |
| N4 | villus epithelium | 81% enterocytes (FABP2, CES2); the villi at the top |
| N5 | crypts | cycling TAs, enteroendocrine and goblet cells, OLFM4; the crypt band below the villi |
| N6 | secretory epithelium | only 12 cells: enteroendocrine and goblet cells (ITLN1, RETNLB) |
| N7 | colonic crypts | no cells in 147328 |
| N8 | colonic surface epithelium | no cells in 147328 |

The H&E check covers only the section you have open, 147328 (ileum). N7 and N8 are empty there, so I named them from their gene programs only. N8's are typical of colonic surface cells (SLC26A3, CEACAM5/7). N7's (CD24, SLC26A2, SELENBP1) suggest colonic crypts, but I haven't seen where they sit. They most likely belong to the other section of the ileum_colon project. Open that section in the app and I'll check them on its H&E.

I proposed the region "mucosa" for section 147328. It's waiting in the STAnnotator review window and is added only when you click Accept; you can edit the outline afterwards.

- **What it is:** one piece of 3.76 mm² holding about 29,600 cells. That's 64% epithelial, 15% fibroblasts, 8% T and NK cells, then endothelial, myeloid and mast cells.
- **How I made it:** I outlined the area where epithelial cells and telocytes (the fibroblasts just under the epithelium) are dense, with holes filled. It takes in 99% of those cells. My first try stopped short of the crypt bases on the right, so I widened the reach to 60 µm.
- **Check against the H&E:** the top edge follows the villus tips. The bottom edge runs along the muscularis mucosae, from about row J–K on the left to F–G on the right, so the lamina propria between and below the crypts is inside.

Two things to look at when you review:
- **Lower left:** a dense lymphoid patch at J–K, columns 1–6, is only partly inside. It may be a lymphoid aggregate crossing into the submucosa.
- **Right edge:** around columns 20–24, rows F–H, the edge may sit slightly high of the crypt bottoms.

items.title: Enteroendocrine cells hold stem and Paneth cells
items.text: 2013 cells (11% of epithelium) are called enteroendocrine, but only one sub-cluster (476) carries NEUROD1/SCGN/SCG5/FEV. The others are LGR5/ASCL2/SMOC2/EPHB3+ crypt-base cells and an ITLN2-high (92%), REP15/GUCA2A/KLK12+ Paneth-like group. Stem cells get 0 cells because the rule requires all four stem markers plus MKI67-; Paneth cells are missing from the list. Revise the list: Stem cells on LGR5|ASCL2|SMOC2, a Paneth cells type on ITLN2 with REP15, EEC on NEUROD1|SCGN|FEV|CHGB.

action.request: Draft a revised marker list (Stem cells on LGR5|ASCL2|SMOC2, Paneth cells on ITLN2 REP15, EEC on NEUROD1|SCGN|FEV|CHGB), check it and offer it with propose_marker_list

items.title: Cycling TAs is a crypt catch-all
items.text: 6171 cells (11% of all cells) are Cycling TAs, but MKI67/TOP2A are detected in only 34%. Sub-clusters: 1387 truly cycling (MKI67/TOP2A 69%), 1402 APOB/MGAM enterocyte-like, 746 goblet-like (REP15, RETNLB, SPINK4) and 560 LGR5/ASCL2 stem-like. Read the type as crypt epithelium, or require MKI67|TOP2A in the rule so the rest go to enterocytes, goblet and stem cells.

items.title: NK cells are mostly gd T IELs
items.text: In the 314 'NK cells', CD3E is detected in 47% and TRDC in 56% (4% in other T/NK); 204 sit in the epithelium (median 7 um). These are gd T intraepithelial lymphocytes, while gd T cells hold only 11 cells. A further 110 deep cells carry fibroblast/muscle genes (SFRP2, GREM1, ACTG2). Revise: gd T cells on TRDC with CD3E, NK cells requiring CD3E- with KLRF1.

items.title: Monocytes in the mucosa look like cDC2
items.text: The Dendritic cells rule requires CLEC9A, CLEC10A, LAMP3 and CCR7 together, so only LAMP3+CCR7+ mregDCs pass (CLEC10A 6%). The 'Monocytes' meanwhile show CLEC10A 37%, ITGAX 78% and CD14 only 23%; their mucosal majority has no monocyte programme, and a cycling IDO1+ sub-cluster of 155 is DC-like. Only the deep submucosal sub-cluster (234, FCN1/CD14) looks like monocytes. Split Dendritic cells into cDC1 (CLEC9A), cDC2 (CLEC10A) and mregDC (LAMP3, CCR7).

items.title: Mast cells in the muscularis are smooth muscle
items.text: 141 'Mast cells' sit deep in the muscularis propria (median 2.2 mm) with DES 92%, MYH11 96%, ACTG2 89%, and cluster tightly (6.9x). These are smooth muscle cells (or KIT+ ICC, which get 0 cells because the ICC rule excludes CPA3) rather than mast cells. Look at KIT and ANO1 in the muscularis; if ANO1 is there, drop CPA3- from the ICC rule.

items.title: Naive CD4 T cells are unreliable
items.text: Only 134 cells; CCR7 21%, SELL 10%, and their top genes are LAMP3, CCL19, FSCN1 (mregDC genes), with 0.29 confusion against effector/memory CD4. Merge them into CD4 T cells or leave them uninterpreted.

items.title: Epithelial spillover into lamina propria
items.text: Epithelial markers are detected in 42.5% of non-epithelial cells within 10 um of the epithelium vs 6% beyond 60 um, and telocytes' top genes include FABP2, KRT8, CHP2. Keep this in mind for DE or communication between lamina propria cells: epithelial genes there are spillover, not expression.

items.title: Registration holds
items.text: Cells sit on their nuclei: max offset 2.1 um, residual 0.6 um, correlation 0.52 across 40 windows. No correction needed.

items.title: Enteroendocrine cells hold stem and Paneth cells
items.text: 2013 cells (11% of epithelium) are called enteroendocrine, but only one sub-cluster (476) carries NEUROD1/SCGN/SCG5/FEV. The others are LGR5/ASCL2/SMOC2/EPHB3+ crypt-base cells and an ITLN2-high (92%), REP15/GUCA2A/KLK12+ Paneth-like group (572). Stem cells get 0 cells because the rule requires all four stem markers plus MKI67-; Paneth cells are missing from the list. Revise the list: Stem cells on LGR5|ASCL2|SMOC2, a Paneth cells type on ITLN2 with REP15, EEC on NEUROD1|SCGN|FEV|CHGB.

items.title: Cycling TAs is a crypt catch-all
items.text: 6171 cells (11% of all cells) are Cycling TAs, but MKI67/TOP2A are detected in only 34%. Sub-clusters: 1387 truly cycling (MKI67/TOP2A 69%), 1402 APOB/MGAM enterocyte-like, 746 goblet-like (REP15, RETNLB, SPINK4) and 560 LGR5/ASCL2 stem-like. Read the type as crypt epithelium, or require MKI67|TOP2A in the rule so the rest go to enterocytes, goblet and stem cells.

items.title: NK cells are mostly gd T IELs
items.text: In the 314 'NK cells', CD3E is detected in 47% and TRDC in 56% (4% in other T/NK); 204 sit in the epithelium (median 7 um). These are gd T intraepithelial lymphocytes, while gd T cells hold only 11 cells. A further 110 deep cells carry fibroblast/muscle genes (SFRP2, GREM1, ACTG2). Revise: gd T cells on TRDC with CD3E, NK cells requiring CD3E- with KLRF1.

items.title: cDC2 are labelled Monocytes
items.text: Dendritic cells hold cDC1 (112, CLEC9A) and mregDC (92, CCR7) but no cDC2: CLEC10A is in 6% of DCs. The 'Monocytes' show CLEC10A 37%, ITGAX 78% and CD14 only 23%; their mucosal majority (443) has no monocyte programme, and a cycling IDO1+ group (155) is DC-like. Only the deep submucosal sub-cluster (234, FCN1 72%, CD14 53%) looks like monocytes. Add cDC2 (CLEC10A) under Dendritic cells.

items.title: Mast cells in the muscularis are smooth muscle
items.text: 141 'Mast cells' sit deep in the muscularis propria (median 2.2 mm) with DES 92%, MYH11 96%, ACTG2 89%. They may be smooth muscle cells or KIT+ ICC (0 cells, the ICC rule excludes CPA3).

items.title: Naive CD4 T cells are unreliable
items.text: Only 134 cells; CCR7 21%, SELL 10%, top genes LAMP3, CCL19, FSCN1 (mregDC genes), confusion 0.29 with effector/memory CD4. Merge into CD4 T cells or leave uninterpreted.

items.title: Epithelial spillover into lamina propria
items.text: Epithelial markers are detected in 42.5% of non-epithelial cells within 10 um of the epithelium vs 6% beyond 60 um, and telocytes' top genes include FABP2, KRT8, CHP2. In DE or communication between lamina propria cells, treat epithelial genes there as spillover, not expression.

items.title: Registration holds
items.text: Max offset 2.1 um, residual 0.6 um, correlation 0.52 over 40 windows. No correction needed.

- **Review candidates:** all 8 candidate areas were false alarms. On the H&E each is smooth muscle in real muscle (vessel walls, muscularis mucosae strands, muscularis propria). Of the 26 marker checks I kept 6 as real: Cycling TAs, enteroendocrine cells, naive CD4 T cells, NK cells, monocytes and dendritic cells. The rest are low-detected or pan-lineage markers on types that are otherwise well defined.
- **Advice kept (4 taxonomy, 1 QC):** only 476 of the 2,013 enteroendocrine cells look enteroendocrine; the rest are crypt-base stem cells (LGR5/ASCL2) and Paneth-like cells (ITLN2), and the list has no Paneth type. Only about a third of Cycling TAs express MKI67, so the label covers crypt epithelium in general. Most NK cells are γδ T cells in the epithelium (CD3E 47%, TRDC 56%). The mucosal monocytes look like cDC2, which the DC class lacks. Epithelial transcripts spill into lamina propria cells next to the epithelium (42.5% within 10 µm vs 6% beyond 60 µm).
- **Dropped:** "mast cells in the muscularis are smooth muscle" (it could equally be smooth muscle signal leaking into real mast cells), naive CD4 T cells (only 134 cells, already shown as a marker check), and registration (2.1 µm at most, nothing to fix).

The annotation and analyses are unchanged. The kept items are in the app's Review panel.

items.title: Rerun with a curated resource
items.text: The run used resource 'all', whose OmniPath consensus adds pairs that are not ligand-receptor biology and that now lead the result: MYL9→CD69 (myosin light chain; the 'other' pathway, 220 hits, Smooth muscle → ILCs/NK/T), TGFB1→CXCR4 (the top 'TGFb' pathway, score 38), CXCL8→CD79A, MMP2→PECAM1 and C3→ITGAX. With CellChatDB alone (42 pairs on the panel, 328 significant) all of these vanish and TGFb falls to 0.8. Rerun with CellChatDB (or CellPhoneDB) before interpreting.

items.title: PECAM1 adhesion tops the list; look past it
items.text: PECAM1→PECAM1 between endothelial cells, pericytes and passing leukocytes fills most of the top ranks in both resources and in every region. It reflects that these cells line the same vessels, not a regulated signal. The canonical signals that survive CellChatDB are PDGFB→PDGFRB (blood vessel EC → pericytes; glia → trophocytes), CCL5→ACKR1 (CD8 T cells → ACKR1+ venular EC, 3118 neighbour pairs) and NCAM1 between enteric neurons and glia; start there.

items.title: Some senders/receivers are mislabelled types
items.text: Pairs that involve NK cells, Monocytes or Naive CD4 T cells inherit open annotation problems: CCL19→CCR7 'Naive CD4 T → Dendritic cells' rests on CCL19 in naive CD4 T cells, whose top genes are mregDC genes (LAMP3, CCL19, FSCN1); 'Monocytes' receivers are largely cDC2-like; 'NK cells' are mostly gd T IELs. Fix these types (annotation review) before reading their interactions.

Mostly the ileum section (147328). Both sections are non-IBD diverticulitis controls, so don't expect inflammation, and the colon section's epithelium needs a colon marker list before anything there can be read.

**Worth a look in 147328 (terminal ileum)**

1. **A lymphoid follicle with its T-cell zone.** B cells cluster with naive CD4 T cells, ILCs and CCR7+/LAMP3+ dendritic cells. Tregs also sit next to those dendritic cells more than expected (log2 2.6). The B cells lie deep, about 140 µm from the muscle and 240 µm from the epithelium, which fits a follicle reaching through the muscularis mucosae; Peyer's patches are typical of the terminal ileum.
